c.tagline: Duty-free shopping, Danish colonial lanes, and a pirate harbor on the U.S. Virgin Islands' busiest cruise coast.

taxi.fareNote: No Uber or ride-hailing. Shared open-air 'safari' taxi-vans and sedans charge government-set per-person rates by zone (published in the Virgin Islands taxi tariff); confirm the fare and whether it is per person before boarding.

emergency.note: 911 is the island-wide emergency line for police, fire, and medical; the U.S. Virgin Islands are a U.S. territory.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

solo.f: fine by day; avoid dark streets

hood_landmark.Historic Downtown: Main Street Charlotte Amalie St Thomas

avoid.reason: Avoid the Savan neighborhood and unlit backstreets uphill from the waterfront after dark, where most of the town's street crime occurs.
Downtown empties quickly once cruise ships depart; don't linger in deserted alleys or on Main Street late at night.

hood_desc: The compact Danish-colonial core between Veterans Drive and Government Hill — Main Street's duty-free shops, Emancipation Garden, Fort Christian, the 99 Steps, and Blackbeard's Castle on the hill above; the most walkable, sightseeing-rich base.

A small waterfront fishing quarter just west of downtown settled by St-Barth 'French' families, now the town's best pocket for seafood restaurants, casual bars, and sunset drinks; lively after dark yet low-key.

A resort strip on the headland southeast of town wrapping Morningstar and Frenchman's Reef beaches, with big beachfront hotels, pools, and harbor views; best for a sand-and-sea stay near the cruise action.
A calm beach cove right beside Cyril E. King Airport and the Crown Bay cruise dock, with a couple of low-key beachfront hotels; convenient for quick arrivals and departures.
The far-eastern tip of St. Thomas around the Red Hook ferry harbor, ringed by quieter beach resorts, marinas, and the departure point for St. John; relaxed and residential, a short drive from town.
lodging: The Westin Beach Resort & Spa at Frenchman's Reef
Buoy Haus Beach Resort at Frenchman's Reef

water.note: Municipal and cistern supplies are treated but variable, so most visitors drink bottled water.

transit.hours: VITRAN buses run roughly 5:30 AM to 7-8 PM with limited, infrequent service; 'safari' vans run through the day. After dark, taxis are the only real option.
transit.note: St. Thomas has no rail or metro. Public transit is limited to infrequent VITRAN buses and privately-run open-air 'safari' taxi-vans, so most visitors get around by taxi. Ferries from Red Hook and downtown connect to St. John and the other Virgin Islands.
transit.pay: VITRAN public buses cost about $1 (75¢ for seniors and students), paid in cash to the driver. Open-air 'safari' taxi-vans on the main routes charge government-set per-person rates (about $1-2 within town). There is no rechargeable transit card.

car.idp: Not required (U.S. and most foreign licenses accepted); note that driving is on the LEFT.

landmarks: Magens Bay
A mile-long heart-shaped arc of powder sand and calm turquoise water framed by green peninsulas, perennially ranked among the world's most beautiful beaches.
Fort Christian
The Virgin Islands' oldest standing structure, a russet-red Danish fortress begun in 1666, now a museum anchoring Charlotte Amalie's historic waterfront.
99 Steps
A brick staircase built from Danish ship-ballast in the 1700s climbs Government Hill past colonial mansions to sweeping harbor views, actually numbering 103 steps.
Paradise Point Skyride
Gondolas glide 700 feet above the harbor to a mountaintop deck where banana daiquiris accompany the definitive panorama of cruise ships and emerald islands.
St. Thomas Synagogue
Founded in 1796, the Western Hemisphere's second-oldest synagogue in continuous use retains its symbolic sand floor and graceful mahogany interior.
Emancipation Garden
The historic square where the 1848 proclamation freeing the Danish West Indies' enslaved people was read, marked by a Liberty Bell replica and bandstand.
Blackbeard's Castle (Skytsborg Tower)
A 1679 Danish watchtower atop Government Hill, steeped in pirate legend, presiding over one of the Caribbean's finest natural-harbor views.
Drake's Seat
A roadside mountain overlook where Sir Francis Drake supposedly surveyed his fleet, now the classic photo stop above heart-shaped Magens Bay.
Mountain Top
St. Thomas's highest accessible viewpoint at 1,500 feet claims the invention of the banana daiquiri and views spanning twenty islands and cays.
Coral World Ocean Park
At Coki Point, an undersea observatory, sea lion encounters, and reef pools bring the Caribbean's marine life within arm's reach of visitors.

train.note: There is no railway in the US Virgin Islands. Arrive by air into Cyril E. King airport on St Thomas, which has direct flights from the US mainland and Puerto Rico, or by ferry and cruise ship.

bus.note: No international coaches. VITRAN buses run the length of St Thomas from Charlotte Amalie for a low flat fare, though services are infrequent; open-air safari taxis and shared vans are far more common and stop anywhere along the route. Taxis charge fixed per-person rates published by the tourism board.

ferry.note: The BVI crossings are international sailings with US and British immigration at either end, so carry your passport. The St John ferry from Red Hook, on the eastern end of St Thomas, runs roughly hourly and is the standard way to reach the national park island; a less frequent service also leaves from Charlotte Amalie itself. Schedules are reduced on Sundays.

half.name: St. John (Virgin Islands National Park)
half.blurb: A short ferry ride to an island where most of the land is protected parkland, with Trunk Bay's famous underwater snorkel trail.

half.name: Tortola
half.blurb: The largest of the BVI, reachable by ferry, with hillside villages, Cane Garden Bay and views across the Sir Francis Drake Channel.

half.name: Virgin Gorda
half.blurb: Home to The Baths, a maze of giant granite boulders forming grottoes and tidal pools along a turquoise shoreline.

full.name: St. Croix
full.blurb: The largest USVI island, with the Danish colonial town of Christiansted and the underwater trail at Buck Island Reef.
